title: Symphony No. 4 in E-flat major, “Romantic”
hook: A horn call at daybreak, a hunt in the forest, and a nickname Bruckner chose himself.

painting.title: Medieval City on a River
painting.pairingNote: A Gothic cathedral, a castle on the hill and a procession of riders below, the dream of the Middle Ages that Bruckner’s own programme for the symphony describes, with a city at daybreak and knights riding out.

facts: Bruckner wrote the symphony in 1874 and kept reworking it for more than a decade. In 1878 he replaced the scherzo with a new “hunt” scherzo, and in 1879–80 he composed a new finale. This revised version was first performed on 20 February 1881 in Vienna, conducted by Hans Richter, and it was a success. It was the first premiere of a Bruckner symphony that he did not conduct himself.

The nickname “Romantic” is Bruckner’s own. Later, in letters, he sketched a programme: in the first movement a horn announces the day from the town hall; the second theme is the song of a great tit; the scherzo is a hunt, and its trio a dance tune played during the hunters’ meal in the forest. A friend passed on a fuller version, with a medieval city at daybreak, gates opening and knights riding out into the forest.
Bruckner was an organist, and it shows: the orchestra often works in blocks, strings, woodwinds and brass taking turns like the stops of an organ. The horns lead almost everywhere.
A rhythm runs through the symphony: two notes, then three in the same time. It is so typical of him that it is called the [[bruckner-rhythm|Bruckner rhythm]].
bigPicture.inOneLine: daybreak and a horn call (I), a slow walk and a song (II), a hunt with a country dance in the middle (III), a vast finale that ends with the opening horn call (IV).

movements.heading: Bewegt, nicht zu schnell
movements.summary: Out of a soft shimmer of strings, a single horn calls. That call is the seed of the movement, and of the whole symphony. Like most of Bruckner’s first movements it is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with three groups of themes instead of two, laid out on a huge scale.

mainIdeas.name: The horn call
mainIdeas.description: a falling and rising fifth, played softly by one horn over trembling strings.
The [[bruckner-rhythm|Bruckner rhythm]]: two plus three, hammered out by the full orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The song theme
mainIdeas.description: a lilting melody in D-flat major for the violas, with a little bird call in the violins above.

stops.hear: Strings whisper on one trembling chord; a single horn calls, softly, from far away
stops.happening: The opening: the horn “announces the day”, in Bruckner’s words. The shimmer is a string [[tremolo|tremolo]]

stops.hear: The woodwinds take up the call; the music slowly grows
stops.happening: The first theme spreads through the orchestra

stops.hear: The whole orchestra bursts in, loud, with a stamping two-plus-three rhythm
Sudden calm; the violas sing a lilting tune while the violins chirp above
stops.happening: The second group, in D-flat major. Bruckner said this was the song of a great tit

stops.hear: Brass and full orchestra again, broad and heavy, with the two-plus-three rhythm
stops.happening: The third group, in B-flat major. The end of the [[exposition|exposition]]

stops.hear: The horn call returns quietly and starts to wander through new keys
The brass play a slow, solemn hymn built from the horn call
stops.happening: A brass [[chorale|chorale]] at the heart of the development

stops.hear: The shimmer and the horn call again, now with a flute line weaving around it
The horn call is repeated and repeated, louder each time

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The horns blaze out the call over the whole orchestra in E-flat major
stops.happening: The movement ends in full daylight

notice: Count how often you hear the opening horn call. It returns in the woodwinds, in the brass hymn, in the recapitulation and at the end, and once more at the very end of the symphony.
Listen for the moments when the full orchestra stops dead and a few quiet instruments carry on alone. Organists change stops the same way.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Karl Böhm recorded the symphony with the Vienna Philharmonic in the Sofiensaal in Vienna in November 1973. He plays the 1878–80 version in Leopold Nowak’s edition. Decca first issued it on two LPs in 1974.

movements.heading: Andante quasi allegretto
movements.summary: A slow walk in C minor, not a lament: Bruckner marks it “quasi allegretto”, almost moving along. Two ideas take turns, a sombre song for the cellos and a long, warm melody for the violas over plucked strings. The movement rises to one great climax near the end and then fades away.

mainIdeas.name: The cello song
mainIdeas.description: a sombre melody low in the strings, over a soft, steady tread.

mainIdeas.name: The viola melody
mainIdeas.description: a long, singing line over [[pizzicato|pizzicato]] strings, like a serenade.

stops.hear: Quiet string chords; the cellos sing a sombre melody
stops.happening: The first theme, in C minor

stops.hear: The melody passes to the woodwinds, and a horn answers
stops.happening: The theme continues in new colours

stops.hear: The strings pluck softly while the violas sing a long, warm melody
stops.happening: The second theme. Bruckner called this movement “song, prayer, serenade”

stops.hear: The cello song comes back, with new lines around it
The plucked strings and the viola melody again
The opening song grows, step by step, into a blaze for the whole orchestra in C major

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: The music falls away to a last, distant echo of the song

notice: Listen to the violas when they take the melody. In most symphonies they accompany; here they have the most beautiful tune.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Bewegt – Trio: Nicht zu schnell. Keinesfalls schleppend
movements.tempo: Scherzo: Bewegt – Trio: Nicht zu schnell. Keinesfalls schleppend
movements.summary: Bruckner called it a hunt. Horn calls echo across the orchestra, and the full brass rings out like a hunting party in full cry. In the middle, the [[trio|trio]] is a slow country dance, which Bruckner described as a tune played during the hunters’ meal in the forest. Then the hunt starts again.

mainIdeas.name: The hunting calls
mainIdeas.description: fanfares for the horns, then trumpets and trombones, over rushing strings.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, swaying tune in G-flat major, in the style of an Austrian [[landler|Ländler]].

stops.hear: Rustling strings; the horns call to one another, softly and then louder
The full brass rings out in a blazing fanfare
The fanfares quieten and drift into softer, distant keys
The calls return and build to a second blaze
Slower and gentle: a swaying dance tune in the woodwinds and strings
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]], a [[landler|Ländler]] for the hunters’ meal

stops.hear: The rustling strings and the horn calls again
stops.happening: The scherzo is played again from the start

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The full brass and a sharp final chord

notice: Compare the horns in the scherzo with the dance in the trio. The same orchestra sounds first like an open forest, then like a village inn.

movements.heading: Finale: Bewegt, doch nicht zu schnell
movements.tempo: Finale: Bewegt, doch nicht zu schnell
movements.summary: The longest movement, and the most dramatic. It starts in darkness and works its way, through storms, quiet songs and solemn brass hymns, towards the light. At the end the horn call from the very beginning of the symphony comes back, and the symphony closes in a radiant E-flat major.

mainIdeas.name: The main theme
mainIdeas.description: a huge, stark melody played by the whole orchestra in [[unison|unison]].

mainIdeas.name: The song theme
mainIdeas.description: a gentle melody for the strings, with bird-like woodwinds.
The horn call from the first movement, which returns at the end.

stops.hear: A low, throbbing figure in the strings; horns recall the hunting calls of the scherzo
The whole orchestra hurls out a huge, stark theme together
stops.happening: The main theme, in [[unison|unison]], the first great climax

stops.hear: Calm: the strings sing a gentle melody; woodwinds chirp around it
The full orchestra again, heavy and stamping, with the two-plus-three rhythm
Quiet again; fragments of the themes drift and combine
The stark main theme and the gentle song come back in new forms
A soft, slow hymn in the strings and woodwinds; the music seems to start again from nothing

stops.label: Last 90 seconds
stops.hear: A long climb to the full orchestra; the horns ring out the call from the first movement
stops.happening: The symphony ends where it began, now in full light

notice: In the last pages, listen for the horns. The call that opened the symphony comes back as the final word.

threads.title: The horn
threads.body: It opens the symphony alone, leads the hunt in the scherzo and closes the finale with the opening call. This is a symphony for the horn.

threads.title: Two plus three
threads.body: The [[bruckner-rhythm|Bruckner rhythm]] stamps through the first movement and the finale, a signature as clear as a name.

threads.title: Song and storm
threads.body: Every movement sets a broad, singing tune against massive blocks of brass, and Bruckner names the quiet sections “songs”.

threads.title: The long road
threads.body: Bruckner revised this symphony again and again between 1874 and 1888. What you hear is one stage of that journey, the version that made it a success.
